items.title: ‘Physical: Asia’ Season 2 Is Officially Happening, and It’s Building an Entirely New World
items.summary:
Summary 

Netflix confirms Physical: Asia Season 2 will premiere in 2027.The season promises culture-inspired quests and nation-versus-nation matchups.The unscripted athletic survival franchise continues its rapid global expansion.

Netflix has confirmed that Physical: Asia will return for a second season in 2027, bringing back the competition in which Asian nations battle for national pride.

The series first premiered in October 2025 as the franchise’s first international team format, moving the action from individual athletes to national squads taking on large-scale quests inspired by Asian cultures. That combination of grit, teamwork and sportsmanship helped the Physical brand extend its streak in Netflix’s Global Top 10 to three consecutive seasons.

Producer Jang Ho-gi says the new season will not simply be a bigger version of the first. “For Season 2, we have designed an entirely different world from previous installments and developed quests capable of becoming new signatures for the Physical series,” he said, adding that the team plans to introduce new strategies, matchups and surprise results that only a nation-versus-nation format can produce.

The renewal is the latest sign of how far the franchise has traveled since Physical: 100 debuted in South Korea in early 2023. Local adaptations Physical: 100: Mexico and Physical: 100: Italy each held a spot in the Global Top 10 for two straight weeks, the Mexican edition has already been renewed for a second season, and U.S., French and Swedish versions are in development.

Kihwan Yoo, Director of Content at Netflix…
items.t: ‘Physical: Asia’ Season 2 Is Officially Happening, and It’s Building an Entirely New World

items.title: Van Gogh's "Blossoming Chestnut Trees" Sells for $190.4 Million USD, Becoming the Fourth Priciest Auction Sale Ever
items.summary:
Summary 

Vincent van Gogh’s 1890 masterpiece has achieved a staggering $190.4 million at a recent Sotheby's auction in ManhattanThe monumental transaction not only sets a new record for the artist but also ranks as the fourth most expensive art sale in auction historyThe historic sale successfully proceeded after a confidential eleventh-hour settlement regarding a Nazi-era ownership dispute

Sotheby's has officially overseen the historic $190.4 million sale of Vincent van Gogh 's "Châtaigniers en Fleurs (Blossoming Chestnut Trees)." The monumental Manhattan transaction establishes a massive new auction record for the legendary artist and officially cements the masterpiece as the fourth priciest sale ever recorded in auction history.

"Blossoming Chestnut Trees" offers a poignant glimpse into the final chapter of the artist's life. The record-breaking 1890 canvas beautifully depicts the serene French village of Auvers, capturing the light-dappled pastoral setting where van Gogh spent his final months before his death. The luminous scene of a large chestnut tree blooming in the evening light stands as a profound testament to his late-stage creative output, ultimately becoming the crown jewel of the Blaquier-Arrieta collection.

The historic sale arrived with intense eleventh-hour drama, proceeding only after a confidential settlement was reached regarding an ownership dispute tied to Nazi persecution in the 1930s. Defying a cautious high-end art market, the piece was ultimately acquired by veteran art dealer William Acquavella, securing its unprecedented final price tag and…
items.t: Van Gogh's "Blossoming Chestnut Trees" Sells for $190.4 Million USD, Becoming the Fourth Priciest Auction Sale Ever

items.title: A Coyote-Powered 1969 Ford Bronco Has Been Auctioned
items.summary:
Summary 

A fully customized 1969 Ford Bronco is currently up for auction via dealer consignmentThe classic truck is powered by a modern 5.0-liter Coyote V8 engine rated at 420 horsepowerThe extensive build features a lifted suspension with Fox shocks alongside four-wheel disc brakes and a bespoke interior

Ford 's iconic off-roader gets a massive modern upgrade in this custom 1969 Ford Bronco , which is currently up for auction at Bring A Trailer . Completed over a nine-year build process between 2013 and 2022, the vintage 4x4 masterfully blends classic American truck aesthetics with contemporary performance hardware and off-road capability.

Under the hood, the restomod replaces its original powertrain with a modern 5.0-liter Coyote crate V8 sourced from Summit Racing, pushing out an impressive 420 horsepower. The engine is mated to a Blumenthal five-speed manual transmission and an Atlas 3.0:1 Highlander dual-range transfer case. Delivering power to the ground, the Bronco sits on a lifted suspension system equipped with front Pro Comp coil springs, a rear multi-link coilover conversion utilizing Fox shocks, and a Currie Antirock sway bar. Stopping power is handled by four-wheel disc brakes featuring an Explorer-style rear setup and a hydroboosted Wilwood master cylinder.

Aesthetically, the body was repaired and refinished in a sleek gloss black, contrasting heavily with a removable white hardtop, white bumpers, and white 17-inch smoothie-style wheels wrapped in BFGoodrich All-Terrain T/A KO2 tires. Rugged exterior additions include a Warn winch, flush-fit hood pins,…

items.title: The Long Game: How Robert Pattinson Built the Perfect Resume for James Bond
items.summary:
Robert Pattinson ’s ascension to the role of James Bond is not just a major casting announcement—it is the culmination of one of the most calculated and successful career reinventions in modern Hollywood history. After officially being tapped by Amazon-MGM as the seventh actor to don the iconic tuxedo, the 40-year-old British star is set to usher 007 into a highly anticipated new era.

The blueprint of Pattinson's career is a masterclass in defying expectations. After exploding into global superstardom as the brooding vampire Edward Cullen in the Twilight franchise, he fiercely refused to be boxed in as a standard-issue Hollywood heartthrob. Instead, he spent the better part of a decade retreating into the gritty, auteur-driven trenches of independent cinema. Through daring, transformative performances in the Safdie brothers’ breathless Good Time and Robert Eggers’ surreal, claustrophobic The Lighthouse , Pattinson stripped away his teen-idol sheen and rebuilt his reputation as a character actor of remarkable range and feral intensity.

Having secured his indie credibility, he executed a flawless pivot back to the blockbuster stage. As the angsty, detective-focused Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves’ The Batman (2022), Pattinson proved he could anchor a massive global franchise without compromising his artistic edge. His recent winning streak—earning "Oscar-worthy" acclaim as a real-life TV host in Primetime , stealing scenes as the villainous Antinous in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , and teaming up with Denis Villeneuve for Dune: Part Three —has solidified his status as a…
items.t: The Long Game: How Robert Pattinson Built the Perfect Resume for James Bond

PGA Tour legend Tiger Woods is officially making his return to the green for the upcoming Hero World Challenge. Stepping back into the spotlight after a grueling two-year absence, the 15-time major champion announced Tuesday that he will compete in the 72-hole, no-cut tournament set to take place at the Albany Golf Club in New Providence, Bahamas.

The 50-year-old golf legend hosts the annual tournament, which directly benefits his TGR Foundation. Joining a 20-man field that now includes recent additions Gary Woodland and Rickie Fowler, Woods will take on the strenuous 72-hole event from December 3 to December 6, where players are strictly prohibited from using golf carts.

The impending December tee time marks Woods' first PGA Tour appearance since missing the cut at the 2024 Open Championship at Scotland's Royal Troon Golf Club. His extended time away from the sport was initially prompted by a ruptured Achilles tendon in his left leg ahead of the 2025 Masters, which forced him to miss the entire season. This was followed by a seventh back surgery in October 2025 to replace a disk in his lower back. items.title: How Citizen Turned Five Decades of Light Powered Energy Into Everyday Fashion and Modern Luxury with Eco-Drive
items.summary:
Fifty years after Citizen  revolutionized timekeeping with the 1976 Crystron Solar Cell, light-powered watches* have evolved from a bold answer to an energy crisis into a central pillar of modern style. Today, roughly 80% of Citizen timepieces are powered by Eco-Drive technology — a testament to a five-decade obsession with eliminating disposable batteries without sacrificing aesthetic flair. Over those 50 years, relentless engineering has slashed light-transmission requirements from 80% down to under 15%, giving designers total creative freedom while packing movements with atomic-level precision and power reserves that run up to a full year in total darkness.

What started as pure technical problem-solving now strikes a chord with contemporary culture, particularly among a wide generation of audiences. Today’s landscape is shaped by conscious consumerism, where young buyers look for traditional, stylish wristwatches that seamlessly align with sustainable values. Fueled by a data-first approach and a deep digital transformation, light-powered horology has captured new and veteran watch fans as its fastest-growing demographic, proving that environmental mindfulness and individual self-expression go hand in hand.

Within streetwear culture - a world obsessed with the intersection of functional utility and high-concept design - this fifty-year evolution feels entirely at home. Sleek integrated bracelets, sharp geometric silhouettes, and ultra-durable Super Titanium™ treated with scratch-resistant Duratect coatings directly mirror the modern technical aesthetic. High-tech dial…
items.t: How Citizen Turned Five Decades of Light Powered Energy Into Everyday Fashion and Modern Luxury with Eco-Drive

items.title: What Went Down at the Inaugural Hypegolf Social Club, Powered by Toyota
items.summary:
Hypegolf Social Club is built on a simple idea: the best way to get into golf is to play it. Golf has a well-earned reputation for being notoriously stiff. Between the strict dress codes, the obsession with handicaps, and the unspoken rules, getting into the game can feel like navigating a minefield. And Hypegolf Social Club was built to completely flip that script.

On November 14, that exact energy took over the Scholl Canyon Golf Club in Los Angeles. Powered by the Toyota Grand Highlander and Toyota RAV4, the inaugural LA event stripped away the sport's usual intimidation factor and replaced it with a heavy focus on community, gear and a genuinely good time.

Scholl Canyon was the perfect venue for this blueprint. The 18-hole executive course plays shorter than a standard layout and has a driving range on site. Rounds move quickly and the game feels approachable from the first tee, which made it a natural fit for an event designed with newer players in mind. When doors opened at 1 p.m., a 200-person crowd rolled up. The turnout featured a true cross-section of the culture, with scratch players warming up right next to people gripping a club for the literal first time.

The afternoon was built to bring everyone together and get them playing, whatever their experience level. Out on the links, experienced players locked into a fast-paced, nine-hole scramble. At the same time, newcomers linked up with Toyota Pros rocking custom caddie bibs for real-time clinics on tee shots and short-game fundamentals.

items.title: The Brand Crossovers That Shaped Culture in 2026
items.summary:
In 2026, the most interesting collaborations didn't stay in their lane. A football federation gave its kit to a Paris designer. A pop star turned a halftime look into a high-street wardrobe. Lunazul Tequila and a New York designer found a shared muse in the moon, and translated the spirit of blue weber agave into a moonlit runway capsule.

The common thread was context. The pairings that mattered this year were tied to moments people were already living through: a home World Cup, a championship parade down Broadway, a festival debut, a fashion week under the Unisphere. They gave fans something to wear to the moment, not just something to collect.

Below, we look back at the brand crossovers that shaped culture in 2026, where fashion met sport, music and lifestyle, and both sides came out bigger for it.

LUAR x Lunazul Tequila 

Few pairings this year shared a muse quite so literally. "Luar" means moonlight in Galician and Portuguese, and Lunazul translates to "blue moon" in Spanish, a connection Raul Lopez summed up simply: "The moon brings people together." From there, the collaboration became a study in shared craft. Lopez stepped away from New York to visit an agave farm and follow the plant from seed to sewing machine, then built the capsule around vegan agave leather, a plant-based material that echoes the blue weber agave at the heart of Lunazul's tequila, a craft the brand has honed for more than seven generations. Lunazul's signature blue runs through the contrast stitching and leather details against deep black denim: black for the night sky, blue for the moon…
items.t: The Brand Crossovers That Shaped Culture in 2026

items.title: F1 Drivers Will Now Race With WHOOP Strapped to Their Biceps

WHOOP is now the first consumer wearable the FIA has approved for use during a Formula 1 raceDrivers wear the band on the bicep inside a specially designed fire-resistant sleeve for continuous physiological monitoringStarting in 2027, WHOOP Live will feed real-time data from participating drivers into the F1 broadcast

WHOOP has signed a four-year global partnership with Formula 1 , becoming the sport’s Official Health & Fitness Wearable Partner and the first consumer wearable the FIA has cleared for in-race use. The band makes its race debut at this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, the first time F1 drivers have been allowed to wear WHOOP while competing.

Getting the wearable into the cockpit meant rethinking where it sits on the body. Instead of the wrist, participating drivers wear WHOOP on the bicep, held in a fire-resistant sleeve designed specifically for racing. The band tracks the body continuously, so it doesn’t stop when the car does. It logs how drivers respond to training, competition, long-haul travel and sleep around the clock. That builds on what the hardware already does for everyday members, with a 14-day battery and guidance across sleep, recovery, strain, fitness and longevity.

The broadcast side is where fans will see it, under the name WHOOP Live. Starting in 2027, real-time physiological data from participating drivers will appear on F1’s coverage through the season. It will show at key moments like the start, a big overtake or the final lap, adding a layer of driver data next to the car telemetry the sport already shows. “Now, for the…

items.title: Vibram Opens the Doors to Its North Brookfield Factory for Second Annual Creator Program
items.summary:
Most people recognize Vibram by the signature yellow octagon on the bottom of their favorite boots, though far fewer have seen where those outsoles actually come from. From November 4 to 6, the brand opened the doors of its US headquarters in North Brookfield, Massachusetts, for the second edition of Made in North Brookfield. This year’s program brought together 15 creators, designers and brand partners from across the US and Canada, including Nicole McLaughlin, Ella Emhoff, Bailey Goldberg, John Chen of ArchivePDF, Gabriele Fazi of Kith and Victoria Wells of Arc’teryx. The three days centered on New England craft and American bootmaking heritage.

North Brookfield is Vibram’s primary US manufacturing center, with factory roots in Massachusetts dating back to 1965. Now owned by Vibram, the plant makes soles for everything from industrial footwear to a classic American boot. It is one of the only rubber outsole factories operating in the US.

The experience kicked off with a tour led by Christopher Nikopoulos, Vibram’s US VP of Operations, following the process from start to finish. In compounding, raw rubber is blended with custom performance formulas and colors. Milling then rolls the rubber into precise sheets, known as “breads,” ready for molding. Finally, in the molding presses, heat and high pressure vulcanize the sheets into finished outsoles with their final shape and tread.

From there, the creators took over. In the boot and sole workshop, each one chose a custom rubber colorway and tread. They worked with either rubber pellets or shapes cut from rubber sheets,…
items.t: Vibram Opens the Doors to Its North Brookfield Factory for Second Annual Creator Program

The city holds significant historical weight for the fashion house, serving as the location where sacai first established its international retail presence with a Central storefront back in 2015 before relocating to the LANDMARK in 2022. The upcoming Spring/Summer 2027 presentation represents a major milestone for the brand as it continues to successfully expand its cultural and retail footprint across the Greater China region.

items.title: Stone Island Brings NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026
items.summary:
Stone Island took NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026, staging a dedicated installation at Capsule Plaza Shanghai @ IYOUTH from November 10 to 15. Designed with Milan studio NM3 , the space marked the installation's China debut following its first outing at Milan Design Week in April.

First launched by Massimo Osti between 1989 and 1994, NO SEASONS returns as a study in a single silhouette. One hooded jacket comes in six proprietary fabrics: Tela Resinata, Nylon Prismatico-TC, Raso Gommato, David-TC, Crinkle Reps NY and Panno. All six are dyed in lead-gray "piombo," so the material does the talking. Standouts include Tela Resinata, an evolution of the brand's foundational Tela Stella canvas, and David-TC, garment-dyed under pressure at up to 130°C for a compressed, textured hand.

NM3 carried that logic into the space. Four powder-coated steel benches, upholstered in the same six fabrics, anchored the room, while the jackets sat on black metal shelving raised to eye level on a new plinth. "NO SEASONS is all about material. And so is our work," NM3 co-founder Nicolò Ornaghi told Hypebeast. "We solve all the design problem[s] basically using one single detail. So it's a metal sheet that is bent and screwed. That's it."
Co-founder Francesco Zorzi saw the same approach in the collection. "It's actually the same attitude that Stone Island operated with in this collection," he said. "It's one jacket, one design, extremely well done, crazy good details, that works all season."

An LED wall screened the collection's new global campaign film by Capsule, while SYLOW, the new Stone…
items.t: Stone Island Brings NO SEASONS to Shanghai Art Week 2026

I haven’t always worn boots. For years I wrote them off – at 5ft 8in, I was convinced anything above the ankle would make my legs look shorter. Then I started wearing them with the right trousers – a straight leg that falls over the top – and realised I’d spent a decade getting winter wrong. All anyone sees is a smart pair of shoes that happens to keep your ankles warm.

Here’s the thing: boots needn’t be intimidating. They’re just the wintry version of the leather shoes you already own. A chelsea is your loafer – it goes with pretty much everything in your wardrobe and every event in your diary, Christmas parties included. A derby boot is laced up, a bit sturdier and just as happy with jeans. The chukka is your weekend trainer. And the chunky, rubber-soled ones? Just think of them as an umbrella for your feet.
